linkedMcqs.explanation: Since Dr. Meera is an assessee (working as a professional) whose accounts are required to be audited under Section 44AB of the Income-tax Act, her due date under Section 139(1) is 31st October of the assessment year.

linkedMcqs.prompt: Was Dr. Meera mandatorily required to file a return of income under Section 139(1) even if her total income was below the basic exemption limit, based on the cash deposit mentioned in the facts?
options: No, because the cash deposit was below Rs. 1 crore.
Yes, because cash deposits in current accounts exceeding Rs. 50,000 trigger mandatory filing.
Yes, because current account cash deposits exceeding Rs. 1 crore trigger mandatory filing under the seventh proviso to Section 139(1).
No, professionals are exempt from the seventh proviso.
linkedMcqs.explanation: The seventh proviso to Section 139(1) mandates return filing if aggregate cash deposits in one or more current accounts exceed Rs. 1 crore. Since Dr. Meera deposited Rs. 1,50,000, which is well below Rs. 1 crore, this specific proviso does not trigger mandatory filing (though she is required to file anyway due to audit requirements and income levels).

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is Dr. Meera liable to pay any late fee under Section 234F for filing her return on 10th November 2026, given that her due date was 31st October 2026?
options: No late fee is payable since she is a professional.
Yes, a late fee of Rs. 5,000 is payable because the return was filed after the due date and her total income exceeds Rs. 5,00,000.
Yes, a late fee of Rs. 1,000 is payable.
No late fee is payable if tax audit report is uploaded on time.
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 234F prescribes a late fee of Rs. 5,000 if the return is furnished after the due date under Section 139(1) and total income exceeds Rs. 5,00,000.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Dr. Meera's tax audit report under Section 44AB is required to be furnished electronically, by what date must it be uploaded?
options: 31st October 2026
30th September 2026
31st July 2026
30th November 2026
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per Rule 6G, the tax audit report under Section 44AB must be furnished electronically at least one month prior to the due date for filing the return of income under Section 139(1). Since the due date is 31st October 2026, the audit report must be uploaded by 30th September 2026.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: Mr. & Mrs. Kapoor are resident individuals. Mr. Kapoor holds financial interest in an entity located in London, United Kingdom. During the financial year 2025-26, Mr. Kapoor's total income computed under the provisions of the Act is Rs. 3,80,000, which is below the basic exemption limit of Rs. 3,00,000 (under the new tax regime, or assume Rs. 2,50,000 under old regime, in either case below basic exemption limit). Mrs. Kapoor's total income is Rs. 6,50,000. Neither of them incurred any high-value electricity expenditure or bank deposits exceeding threshold limits.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Provisions for filing Return of Income and Self Assessment

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is Mr. Kapoor mandatorily required to file a return of income under Section 139(1) for AY 2026-27?
options: No, because his total income is below the basic exemption limit.
Yes, because he is a resident and ordinary resident individual having a financial interest in an entity located outside India.
No, unless the foreign entity distributed dividend during the year.
Yes, because all married individuals must file joint returns.
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under the fourth proviso to Section 139(1), a resident and ordinary resident individual who is a beneficial owner of any asset (including financial interest in any entity) located outside India must mandatorily file a return of income, regardless of their income level.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the due date under Section 139(1) for Mr. Kapoor to file his return of income for AY 2026-27, assuming he is not subject to tax audit?
options: 31st July 2026
31st October 2026
30th November 2026
31st March 2027
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per the explanation to Section 139(1), the due date for filing return of income for an assessee who is required to furnish a report under the fourth proviso (foreign assets) or whose accounts are audited is 31st October of the assessment year.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the due date under Section 139(1) for Mrs. Kapoor to file her return of income for AY 2026-27, assuming she has no foreign assets and is not subject to audit?
options: 31st July 2026
31st October 2026
30th November 2026
31st March 2027
linkedMcqs.explanation: For an individual whose accounts are not required to be audited and who does not have foreign assets, the due date for filing the return of income under Section 139(1) is 31st July of the assessment year.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Mr. Kapoor fails to report his foreign financial interest in his return of income, what penal consequence under the Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015 or Income-tax Act may apply?
options: A flat penalty of Rs. 1,000 under Section 234F.
A penalty of Rs. 10,000 under the Black Money Act / Income-tax Act provisions for non-disclosure.
No penalty if tax on foreign income is nil.
Imprisonment for 7 years without option of fine.
linkedMcqs.explanation: Failure to disclose foreign assets or furnishing inaccurate particulars in the return of income attracts strict penalties, including a penalty of Rs. 10,000 under Section 43 of the Black Money Act (or relevant provisions under Income-tax Act for non-reporting of foreign assets).
